study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative model detects abnormal functional connectivity in psychiatric disorders

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Develop and evaluate a normative model based on autoencoders trained on rs-fMRI data from healthy controls to quantify individual deviations and identify abnormal functional brain network connectivity patterns in SCZ, BD, and ADHD.

The generated difference vectors... reshaped into a 14 × 14 lower triangular matrix, and binarized using the threshold that is defined in the results section... Graph theory was used to obtain the network degree for each subject...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of MSEs using Mann–Whitney tests between test sets; analysis of per-feature MSE (MSEf) matrices and their differences (patients minus healthy) to identify disorder-specific abnormal pairs; graph-theoretic degree comparisons across groups.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Autoencoder-based normative modeling of rs-fMRI functional connectivity identifies disorder-characteristic network abnormalities and generalizes to an independent SCZ dataset, but group-level differences do not robustly translate to individual-level deviations, highlighting disorder heterogeneity.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Basal ganglia network connectivity plays an important role in BD and SCZ, with abnormal BGN–language network connectivity more specific to BD. In SCZ, connections involving higher visual network and right executive control are most relevant; in ADHD, the anterior salience–precuneus connectivity is most relevant. Abnormal connectivity patterns for two independent SCZ groups (UCLA and COBRE) were similar, supporting generalizability. However, group-level differences did not withstand individual-level analysis, implying high heterogeneity across patients.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Unsupervised normative modeling via Keras autoencoder; deviation localization at the level of FBN-pair connectivity with binarization and graph measures; suggests precision-medicine focus on individual network changes over group classification.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: No explicit handling of nuisance structure (e.g., site/scanner, age, motion) beyond standard preprocessing; reliance on MSE deviations without modeling covariates; group-level effects do not translate to individual-level deviations; generalization formally evaluated only for SCZ across sites.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: CoRR healthy subsets used include: BNU3, HNU1, IPCAS1, IPCAS3, IPCAS4, MRN1, NYU2, Utah1, Utah2 (see dataset table). Functional brain networks considered (abbreviations): ASN, AN, BGN, DDMN, HVN, LN, LECN, PSN, PN, PVN, RECN, SN, VDMN, VN (see figure caption). Additional analysis doubled H-Test-U to 78 with corresponding H-Train 327 for robustness.
